## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Arakajātaka* (Ja 169) is a narrative within the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. Set at the Jetavana monastery, the Buddha relates the story in connection with the discourse on loving-kindness (*mettasutta*), opening with the verse beginning *Yo ve mettena cittenā* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].
In the tale of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was born as the religious teacher Araka, who lived in the Himalayan region and instructed many disciples in the development of loving-kindness (*mettābhāvanā*) and related virtues such as benevolence, sympathy, and equanimity [Sahni 2008; Fausböll 1879]. Araka taught that walking this virtuous path leads to companionship with the Brahma world; possessing unbroken absorption (*jhāna*), he was reborn after death in the Brahma-realm (*Brahmaloka*) for seven cosmic cycles (*saṃvattavivaṭṭakappa*) [Sahni 2008; Fausböll 1879]. In the formal identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the gathering of ascetics (*isigaṇa*) as his present assembly of followers and the teacher Araka as himself [Fausböll 1879].
Textual analysis by DharmaNexus identifies eight internal Pali text-reuse matches between the *Arakajātaka* and the *Subha Sutta* of the Majjhima Nikāya (MN 99), sharing phrasing related to the Brahma realms (specifically Ja 169 §2.2–2.4 aligned with MN 99 §24.3 with 0.98 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with score 10 or higher are recorded [DharmaNexus]. The text was edited by V. Fausböll in the second volume of *The Jātaka together with its Commentary*, and SuttaCentral registers four translations across four languages [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].
